parameters.query: select jsonb_object_agg(key, value) as cfg from app_config;

-- "Last sync" node (Postgres, Execute Query). No parameters.
-- For each tool: the date to ask the vendor for usage from = newest stored day minus 2 days
-- (the overlap is safe because usage upserts are idempotent). First run: usage_initial_days back.
-- Also returns run_started_at, used later to resolve findings that were not seen in this run.
SELECT
    now() AS run_started_at,
    jsonb_object_agg(
        lower(split_part(t.name, ' ', 1)),
        to_char(
            COALESCE(
                (SELECT max(u.day) - 2
                 FROM usage_daily u JOIN accounts a ON a.id = u.account_id
                 WHERE a.tool_id = t.id),
                current_date - COALESCE((SELECT (value #>> '{}')::int FROM app_config
                                         WHERE key = 'usage_initial_days'), 120)
            ),
            'YYYY-MM-DD')
    ) AS since
FROM tools t;

-- One row per failed fetch and execution; a re-run of the same execution does not add another.
INSERT INTO dead_letter (workflow, node, payload, error)
SELECT 'A - Usage audit', $1, $2::jsonb, $3
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM dead_letter
    WHERE workflow = 'A - Usage audit' AND node = $1 AND status = 'open'
      AND payload->>'execution_id' = $4
);

parameters.query:
-- "Upsert employees" node. $1 = JSON array from "Normalise employees" ({{ [JSON.stringify($json.employees)] }}).
WITH up AS (
    INSERT INTO employees (email, name, team, cost_center, status, start_date, end_date)
    SELECT e.email, e.name, e.team, e.cost_center, e.status, e.start_date, e.end_date
    FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb) AS e(
        email text, name text, team text, cost_center text,
        status text, start_date date, end_date date)
    ON CONFLICT (email) DO UPDATE SET
        name        = EXCLUDED.name,
        team        = EXCLUDED.team,
        cost_center = EXCLUDED.cost_center,
        status      = EXCLUDED.status,
        start_date  = EXCLUDED.start_date,
        end_date    = EXCLUDED.end_date
    RETURNING (xmax = 0) AS inserted        -- xmax = 0 means the row was newly inserted
)
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE inserted)     AS inserted,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT inserted) AS updated
FROM up;

-- "Rejected to dead_letter" node. $1 = rejected array, $2 = Code node name (e.g. 'Normalise accounts').
-- Same rejected item twice (while still open) is stored once, so re-runs do not pile up.
INSERT INTO dead_letter (workflow, node, payload, error)
SELECT 'A - Usage audit', $2, r.item, r.reason
FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb) AS r(item jsonb, reason text)
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM dead_letter d
    WHERE d.workflow = 'A - Usage audit' AND d.node = $2
      AND d.payload = r.item AND d.status = 'open'
);

-- "Upsert accounts" node. $1 = JSON array from "Normalise accounts".
-- The vendor key ('chatterly', ...) is matched to tools.name by its first word.
WITH up AS (
    INSERT INTO accounts (tool_id, external_id, email, seat_type, status, created_at, last_active_at)
    SELECT t.id, a.external_id, a.email, a.seat_type, a.status, a.created_at, a.last_active_at
    FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb) AS a(
        tool text, external_id text, email text, seat_type text, status text,
        created_at timestamptz, last_active_at timestamptz)
    JOIN tools t ON lower(split_part(t.name, ' ', 1)) = a.tool
    ON CONFLICT (tool_id, external_id) DO UPDATE SET
        email          = EXCLUDED.email,
        seat_type      = EXCLUDED.seat_type,
        status         = EXCLUDED.status,
        created_at     = EXCLUDED.created_at,
        last_active_at = EXCLUDED.last_active_at
    RETURNING (xmax = 0) AS inserted
)
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE inserted)     AS inserted,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT inserted) AS updated
FROM up;

-- "Rejected to dead_letter" node. $1 = rejected array, $2 = Code node name (e.g. 'Normalise accounts').
-- Same rejected item twice (while still open) is stored once, so re-runs do not pile up.
INSERT INTO dead_letter (workflow, node, payload, error)
SELECT 'A - Usage audit', $2, r.item, r.reason
FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb) AS r(item jsonb, reason text)
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM dead_letter d
    WHERE d.workflow = 'A - Usage audit' AND d.node = $2
      AND d.payload = r.item AND d.status = 'open'
);

-- "Upsert usage" node. $1 = one batch (array) from "Normalise usage".
-- Rows whose account is not in the accounts table are counted in "unmatched", not silently lost.
WITH matched AS (
    SELECT a.id AS account_id, u.day, u.activity_count, u.spend_usd
    FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb) AS u(
        tool text, external_id text, day date, activity_count int, spend_usd numeric)
    JOIN tools t    ON lower(split_part(t.name, ' ', 1)) = u.tool
    JOIN accounts a ON a.tool_id = t.id AND a.external_id = u.external_id
),
up AS (
    INSERT INTO usage_daily (account_id, day, activity_count, spend_usd)
    SELECT account_id, day, activity_count, spend_usd FROM matched
    ON CONFLICT (account_id, day) DO UPDATE SET
        activity_count = EXCLUDED.activity_count,
        spend_usd      = EXCLUDED.spend_usd
    RETURNING 1
)
SELECT (SELECT count(*) FROM up) AS upserted,
       jsonb_array_length($1::jsonb) - (SELECT count(*) FROM matched) AS unmatched;

-- "Rejected to dead_letter" node. $1 = rejected array, $2 = Code node name (e.g. 'Normalise accounts').
-- Same rejected item twice (while still open) is stored once, so re-runs do not pile up.
INSERT INTO dead_letter (workflow, node, payload, error)
SELECT 'A - Usage audit', $2, r.item, r.reason
FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb) AS r(item jsonb, reason text)
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM dead_letter d
    WHERE d.workflow = 'A - Usage audit' AND d.node = $2
      AND d.payload = r.item AND d.status = 'open'
);

-- "Audit rules" node (Postgres, Execute Query). No parameters. Read-only: it only SELECTs.
-- Returns one row per finding: finding_type, account_id, employee_email, severity, details.
-- Thresholds come from app_config (see the cfg CTE).
--
-- Email matching (same rule as the data generator): lower-case, and drop any "+tag"
-- so "ana.nikolic+alias@x" is matched to "ana.nikolic@x". That makes alias accounts
-- duplicates, not orphans.
WITH cfg AS (
    SELECT
        COALESCE((SELECT (value #>> '{}')::int     FROM app_config WHERE key = 'inactive_days'),             30) AS inactive_days,
        COALESCE((SELECT (value #>> '{}')::int     FROM app_config WHERE key = 'new_account_grace_days'),    14) AS grace_days,
        COALESCE((SELECT (value #>> '{}')::int     FROM app_config WHERE key = 'mismatch_window_days'),      30) AS window_days,
        COALESCE((SELECT (value #>> '{}')::numeric FROM app_config WHERE key = 'mismatch_min_avg_activity'),  3) AS min_avg
),

-- Every account with its tool and the employee it belongs to (if any).
acct AS (
    SELECT a.id, a.tool_id, lower(split_part(t.name, ' ', 1)) AS tool_key, t.name AS tool_name,
           t.unit_price_monthly AS price, a.external_id, a.email, a.seat_type,
           a.created_at, a.last_active_at,
           regexp_replace(lower(btrim(a.email)), '\+[^@]*@', '@') AS canon_email,
           e.status AS emp_status
    FROM accounts a
    JOIN tools t ON t.id = a.tool_id
    LEFT JOIN employees e ON e.email = regexp_replace(lower(btrim(a.email)), '\+[^@]*@', '@')
),

-- Orphaned: no matching employee, or the employee has left.
orphaned AS (
    SELECT 'orphaned_account' AS finding_type, id AS account_id, email AS employee_email, 'high' AS severity,
           jsonb_build_object(
               'tool', tool_name, 'external_id', external_id, 'seat_type', seat_type,
               'reason', CASE WHEN emp_status IS NULL THEN 'not_in_hr' ELSE 'terminated' END,
               'last_active_at', last_active_at, 'monthly_cost', price) AS details
    FROM acct
    WHERE emp_status IS NULL OR emp_status = 'terminated'
),

-- Inactive: a current employee whose seat has not been used for inactive_days
-- (or never used, and the account is older than the grace period).
inactive AS (
    SELECT 'inactive_seat', a.id, a.email, 'medium',
           jsonb_build_object(
               'tool', a.tool_name, 'external_id', a.external_id, 'seat_type', a.seat_type,
               'last_active_at', a.last_active_at,
               'days_inactive', CASE WHEN a.last_active_at IS NULL THEN NULL
                                     ELSE (current_date - a.last_active_at::date) END,
               'monthly_cost', a.price)
    FROM acct a, cfg
    WHERE a.emp_status = 'active'
      AND ( a.last_active_at < now() - make_interval(days => cfg.inactive_days)
            OR (a.last_active_at IS NULL AND a.created_at < now() - make_interval(days => cfg.grace_days)) )
),

-- Premium seat with a low daily average over the window. Days with no usage row count as zero.
-- Only judged for tools that have usage data in the window (so a failed usage sync cannot
-- flag every premium seat) and for current employees (leavers are already "orphaned").
usage_window AS (
    SELECT u.account_id,
           sum(u.activity_count)::numeric / cfg.window_days   AS avg_daily,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE u.activity_count > 0)        AS active_days
    FROM usage_daily u, cfg
    WHERE u.day > current_date - cfg.window_days
    GROUP BY u.account_id, cfg.window_days
),
tools_with_usage AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT a.tool_id
    FROM usage_daily u JOIN accounts a ON a.id = u.account_id, cfg
    WHERE u.day > current_date - cfg.window_days
),
mismatch AS (
    SELECT 'seat_mismatch', a.id, a.email, 'low',
           jsonb_build_object(
               'tool', a.tool_name, 'external_id', a.external_id, 'seat_type', a.seat_type,
               'avg_daily_activity', round(COALESCE(w.avg_daily, 0), 2),
               'active_days', COALESCE(w.active_days, 0),
               'window_days', cfg.window_days, 'monthly_cost', 0)
    FROM acct a
    CROSS JOIN cfg
    LEFT JOIN usage_window w ON w.account_id = a.id
    WHERE a.seat_type = 'premium'
      AND a.emp_status = 'active'
      AND a.tool_id IN (SELECT tool_id FROM tools_with_usage)
      AND COALESCE(w.avg_daily, 0) < cfg.min_avg
),

-- Duplicate: the same person has 2+ accounts in one tool. The account that uses the person's
-- plain email is kept (then the oldest); each extra one, normally the "+alias", gets a finding
-- (account_id = the extra account), so findings stay unique.
ranked AS (
    SELECT acct.*,
           row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY tool_id, canon_email ORDER BY (lower(btrim(email)) <> canon_email), created_at, id) AS rn,
           first_value(external_id) OVER (PARTITION BY tool_id, canon_email ORDER BY (lower(btrim(email)) <> canon_email), created_at, id) AS kept_external_id
    FROM acct
    WHERE emp_status IS NOT NULL
),
duplicate AS (
    SELECT 'duplicate_account', id, canon_email, 'medium',
           jsonb_build_object(
               'tool', tool_name, 'external_id', external_id, 'email', email,
               'duplicate_of', kept_external_id, 'monthly_cost', price)
    FROM ranked
    WHERE rn > 1
),

-- Over-allocation: more accounts than seats in the contracts that are in force today.
-- Not tied to one account, so employee_email carries "tool:<name>" to keep the key unique per tool.
over_allocation AS (
    SELECT 'over_allocation', NULL::int, 'tool:' || ac.tool_key, 'high',
           jsonb_build_object(
               'tool', ac.tool_name, 'accounts', ac.n_accounts, 'seats', COALESCE(s.seats, 0),
               'excess', ac.n_accounts - COALESCE(s.seats, 0),
               'monthly_cost', (ac.n_accounts - COALESCE(s.seats, 0)) * ac.price)
    FROM (SELECT tool_id, tool_key, tool_name, price, count(*) AS n_accounts
          FROM acct GROUP BY tool_id, tool_key, tool_name, price) ac
    LEFT JOIN (SELECT tool_id, sum(seats) AS seats FROM contracts
               WHERE current_date BETWEEN start_date AND end_date GROUP BY tool_id) s
           ON s.tool_id = ac.tool_id
    WHERE ac.n_accounts > COALESCE(s.seats, 0)
)

SELECT * FROM orphaned
UNION ALL SELECT * FROM inactive
UNION ALL SELECT * FROM mismatch
UNION ALL SELECT * FROM duplicate
UNION ALL SELECT * FROM over_allocation;

-- "Upsert findings" node. $1 = findings array from "Shape findings".
-- A finding seen again only gets last_seen/details refreshed. One that had been resolved and
-- comes back is re-opened and will be notified again.
WITH up AS (
    INSERT INTO audit_findings (finding_type, account_id, employee_email, severity, details)
    SELECT f.finding_type, f.account_id, f.employee_email, f.severity, f.details
    FROM jsonb_to_recordset($1::jsonb) AS f(
        finding_type text, account_id int, employee_email text, severity text, details jsonb)
    ON CONFLICT (finding_type, COALESCE(account_id, 0), COALESCE(employee_email, '')) DO UPDATE SET
        last_seen   = now(),
        severity    = EXCLUDED.severity,
        details     = EXCLUDED.details,
        notified_at = CASE WHEN audit_findings.resolved_at IS NOT NULL THEN NULL
                           ELSE audit_findings.notified_at END,
        resolved_at = NULL
    RETURNING (xmax = 0) AS inserted
)
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE inserted)     AS new_findings,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE NOT inserted) AS seen_again
FROM up;

-- "Resolve findings" node. $1 = run_started_at (from the "Last sync" node).
-- Anything still open that this run did not touch is gone: mark it resolved (history is kept).
UPDATE audit_findings
SET resolved_at = now()
WHERE resolved_at IS NULL
  AND last_seen < $1::timestamptz
RETURNING id;

-- "Select new findings" node. No parameters. Turn on "Always Output Data" in the node settings,
-- otherwise n8n stops here when there are no new findings and the digest never runs.
SELECT f.id, f.finding_type, f.severity, f.employee_email, f.details,
       (SELECT count(*) FROM accounts) AS accounts_checked
FROM audit_findings f
WHERE f.notified_at IS NULL
  AND f.resolved_at IS NULL
ORDER BY f.finding_type, (f.details->>'monthly_cost')::numeric DESC NULLS LAST, f.id;

-- "Mark notified" node, runs after the Slack post succeeds. $1 = finding_ids from "Build digest".
UPDATE audit_findings
SET notified_at = now()
WHERE id = ANY (SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text($1::jsonb)::int)
  AND notified_at IS NULL;
